sentence: This project builds a microscope method that corrects the scattering of light so deep tissue can be imaged.
This project builds genetic risk models that predict who is likely to develop primary open-angle glaucoma, using large genomic datasets.
This project studies how the protein ADAR1 is controlled and what it does in the tumor microenvironment during cancer immunity.
This project tests a technique based on standard clinical MRI scans to find abnormal bone before spine fusion surgery and predict complications.
This project tests whether antibodies that bind vascular amyloid more strongly are more likely to cause vascular side effects in Alzheimer's disease treatment.
This project studies which cells drive periductal fibrosis in primary sclerosing cholangitis, using single-cell analysis of patient tissue.
This project studies how copper enters the developing and adult mammalian brain and what the blood-cerebrospinal barrier does in Wilson disease.
This project studies whether blocking fibroblast growth factor receptors could reduce airway inflammation in cystic fibrosis.
This project uses a systems-based approach to study how carcinogenic chemicals from prior industrial activities affect the human genome and signaling proteins.
This project studies the make-up and function of meningeal ectopic lymphoid tissues that appear in the brain and spinal cord in progressive multiple sclerosis.
This project develops a heart scan that measures myocardial fibrosis in children with cardiomyopathy without a contrast agent.
This project explores whether acidity in xylazine and fentanyl combinations may contribute to severe skin and soft tissue wounds.
This project describes how gastrointestinal problems develop in autistic children and builds machine learning models that predict risk and response to treatment.
This project studies CD4 T cells that become activated at the site of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection and tests a treatment strategy that uses their protection.
This project studies how low density neutrophils cause pulmonary inflammation and abnormal bleeding problems in COVID-19 patients.
This project tries to find out why proteins in photoreceptor neurons get misplaced and cause blindness, and how the cytoskeleton supports the cells.
This project maps genomic organization and function in brain specimens from donors with opioid use disorder and in a cell culture model.
This project studies the biological basis of two molecular phenotypes of sepsis, using immunological, microbial and metabolic measurements.
This project develops optical coherence tomography methods to find imaging biomarkers that predict how age-related macular degeneration progresses.
This project studies how prenatal hypoxia disrupts branched chain amino acid metabolism in neurons, focusing on branched chain amino acid transaminase 1.
